text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 503s and P99 latency observed for hosted inference in us-west-2. Admission queue depth for gpu-pool-7 exceeded threshold. Automatic mitigation engaged.
oncall-bot: Incident channel opened: #incidents — tagging oncall and infra.

Alex P: saw the alert. digging into pool metrics now. queue depth jumped ~10x at 18:01 UTC.

Maria G: KV-cache eviction rate spiked at the same time, lots of prefix cache churn. looks like long-running requests holding locks on the cache entries.

Sam L: interesting — our admission controller uses global counters per-pool. if the head request blocks, others pile up and admission thinks capacity is still available.

Devon R: confirming. logs show many requests stuck in "fetch-kv" for >6s. backend worker threads saturated.

Irene K: is this across all regions or just us-west-2?

Alex P: only us-west-2. us-east and eu are normal. traffic shift from a large customer triggered sudden high-concurrency with long-context prompts.

Jamal T: fallback routing kicked in to smaller quantized variants, but those pools were already at 90% due to sticky-region routing. So we got a tie-back: fallback increased load on secondary pools -> they started queueing too.

Maria G: root cause hypothesis: long-context requests cause synchronous KV-cache locks + admission controller global counters -> head-of-queue lock causes backpressure and then fallback routing amplifies load to other pools.

Sam L: mitigation steps taken: 1) reduced admission threshold for gpu-pool-7 to instant failover, 2) disabled fallback routing to other dedicated pools for affected customer, 3) restarted cache workers on pool hosts to clear stuck locks.

Devon R: commands run:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/fleet-admission --replicas=0 && sleep 2 && kubectl -n inference scale deploy/fleet-admission --replicas=3
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/cache-worker-gpu-pool-7
```

Irene K: after restarts, queue depths dropped back to normal within ~90s and 503s decreased. P99 back to baseline.

ops-bot: Auto-retries were suppressed for the incident window to avoid amplifying load.

Alex P: confirmed metrics: admission rejects rose briefly (intended), token costs decreased as we avoided endless queueing.

Maria G: still seeing elevated RPC error rate between proxy and cache (timeout increased). need a fix to make cache lookups non-blocking for long contexts.

Sam L: short-term change: switch cache lookups to optimistic read path when sequence length > 4096. Will deploy as patch to runtime today.

Jamal T: medium-term: update admission controller to use per-gpu slot accounting instead of a single global counter. reduces head-of-queue single-point-of-failure.

Devon R: also propose per-customer concurrency caps per region to prevent single tenant surges causing cross-pool fallthrough.

Irene K: cost note: the emergency fallback and restarts increased transient GPU-hours. Finance FYI — should be minor but flagging.

Alex P: timeline for postmortem: write-up with graphs + config diffs. Owners below.

Action items:
- Sam L: roll out optimistic cache-read path and monitor (ETA 6h)
- Jamal T: implement per-gpu slot accounting prototype and load-test (ETA 2 weeks)
- Maria G: add instrumentation for per-request cache lock hold time (ETA 3 days)
- Devon R: add per-tenant concurrency caps in routing policy, start with the top 5 tenants (ETA 1 week)
- Irene K: cost impact summary and chargeback suggestion (ETA 3 days)
- Alex P: draft postmortem and publish to #postmortems (ETA EOD)

Maria G: also adding an alert rule to detect long-tailed cache lock hold > 1s at host level.

Alex P: thanks everyone. big lesson: admission counters + blocking cache path = lockstep queueing. need to remove blocking coupling. :white_check_mark:

Irene K: I'll follow up on communication to the customer (ops lead) — heads-up that we throttled fallbacks to stabilize.

Sam L: will post test results for optimistic read by end of shift.

Jamal T: will schedule a runbook update for incident responders on how to disable fallback routing quickly.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved at 18:14 UTC. Root mitigation applied.

Alex P: closing notes: no data exfil, no SLA breach beyond transient 503 spike, fix prioritized. Will attach timeline + graphs to the postmortem doc. :raised_hands:
